text.p: Banque Bruxelles Lambert and its brokerage Vermeulen-Raemdonck on Thursday forecast the Bel-20 share index would reach 1,980 points by the end of 1997.

BBL based its forecast on the assumption that 10-year bond yields would rise to between 6.30 and 6.40 percent, Belgium's gross domestic product (GDP) would rise by 2.2 percent and inflation would remain stable at around 2.1 percent.
The year would be characterised by a progressive switch from a focus on interest rates to a focus on company earnings.

Against this background the bank said it would overweight in its portfolio cyclical shares such as CBR and Petrofina , lightly overweight growth stocks such as UCB and D'Ieteren and underweight interest rate sensitives such as Electrabel and insurers.
The bank said it was neutral on holding companies and retailers, but favoured among them Cobepa , Ackermans & Van Haaren and Delhaize .
Steel stocks Cockerill Sambre and Arbed were for now a 'hold' as second-half 1996 earnings were likely to prove disappointing and the picture was not likely to improve until the second half of 1997.
